original_text: Unbound maintains one authoritative, standardized charity-vetting framework and reusable evidence/status across sponsors. A vetted charity does not undergo duplicate routine vetting solely because another sponsor uses it. Record scope, evidence provenance, effective date and expiry; reverify at least every 180 days, on material changes, and check current sanctions/eligibility at execution. Adverse findings propagate to all affected sponsors. Sponsor-specific grant restrictions and approvals remain distinct from common charity vetting; no self-approved vetting exceptions. Cross-sponsor legal reliance, liability, jurisdictions and recipient classes require counsel validation; model never clears holds.
statement: For every grant, the system MUST evaluate recipient eligibility at two points, approval and payment release, against (a) a current IRS-status observation (TEOS/Pub 78 or EO BMF, plus the Auto-Revocation List) whose retrieval timestamp is no older than the sponsor-configured status-freshness window, and (b) current sanctions screening. It MUST store a per-sponsor, per-grant immutable snapshot of that observation containing the fields required by Rev. Proc. 2018-32 §8.01. A shared cross-sponsor charity evidence record MAY be reused as an input, but each sponsor's reliance snapshot MUST be written to that sponsor's partition. A comprehensive charity review (deep vetting) MUST occur at the sponsor-configured deep-review interval (default 180 days, a sponsor policy and not a legal safe harbor) and on any material-change signal. An expired deep review MUST hold new approvals but MUST NOT be the sole basis for payment-time eligibility.
business_objective: Avoid taxable distributions under IRC 4966 by preserving the sponsor's grant-date reliance under Rev. Proc. 2018-32, while not repeating costly deep vetting for every sponsor.
preconditions: Recipient resolved to a single EIN or a non-US entity record
Sponsor policy version active, defining status_freshness_window and deep_review_interval
inputs: Latest shared IRS-status observation with retrieval timestamp and source file revision date
Latest deep-review record and material-change signals
Supporting-organization type and donor-control certification where applicable
processing_rules: If the IRS-status observation is older than status_freshness_window (a sponsor parameter, owner: sponsor compliance; no default asserted as law), fetch a fresh observation before deciding; if retrieval fails, outcome = Unknown and the grant is held.

Eligible only if the observation shows 509(a)(1)/(2)/(3) public charity status AND not on the Auto-Revocation List AND (if 509(a)(3)) a type that is not non-functionally-integrated Type III AND a current donor-control certification exists for Type I/II/FI-III.
Any recipient outside the excepted classes is routed to expenditure-responsibility or rejection; never auto-approved.
Sanctions: a potential match produces Hold; only an authorized human may disposition a potential match; AI may summarize evidence only.

Write snapshot {sponsorId, grantId, decisionPoint, EIN, name, subsection/509(a) code, supporting-org type, deductibility, source, BMF revision date, retrieval datetime, evidence hash} to the sponsor partition.

Deep review expiry: new approvals Hold with reason DeepReviewExpired; payments for already-approved grants proceed only if the release-time IRS-status and sanctions checks pass and no adverse signal is open.
Adverse signal on a shared charity record creates Hold events for all affected open grants across sponsors within the same commit, without disclosing one sponsor's data to another.
outputs: EligibilityEvaluated event (Eligible | Ineligible | Unknown | Hold) with reasons
postconditions: No payment instruction exists for a grant whose release-time eligibility outcome is not Eligible
Every Eligible outcome has a snapshot retrievable by sponsor and grant
failure_behavior: Data-source outage: Unknown, then Hold. Never treat stale data as current.
Conflicting sources (e.g., Pub 78 vs BMF): Disputed, then Hold, then a human reviewer.
Snapshot write failure aborts the eligibility transaction.
security: Snapshots partitioned by sponsor; shared charity facts contain no sponsor-private data
Only Eligibility component may write EligibilityEvaluated
auditability: Snapshot retained under the tax-reliance retention class (RR-REQ-X-036-r1)
Policy version, data-source revision date and rule trace on every decision
configuration: status_freshness_window (sponsor; must be set before go-live; counsel question Q2)
Additional sponsor restrictions may only make eligibility stricter

advisory: Summarize adverse media or document evidence for a human reviewer
ai_assistance.human_approval_boundary: Any Disputed, Unknown-after-retry, expenditure-responsibility or sanctions potential-match outcome

ui_implications: Grant status shows eligibility dimension with reason and as-of time
Charity profile shows last IRS observation time and deep review date separately
api_implications: Query: GET eligibility/{grantId}?decisionPoint= returns outcome and snapshot reference
Event: EligibilityEvaluated v2 with decisionPoint field; idempotent on (grantId, decisionPoint, policyVersion, observationHash)
Error: 409 EligibilityUnknown when the source is unavailable
reporting_implications: Count of holds by reason and age
Reconstruct as-of eligibility for any grant on any date

acceptance_criteria.given: A charity deep-reviewed 30 days ago whose IRS status is revoked (posted to the Auto-Revocation List) today
acceptance_criteria.when: its approved grant reaches payment release
acceptance_criteria.then: outcome Ineligible, payment held, snapshot records the revocation observation

acceptance_criteria.given: A charity whose deep review expired yesterday and an approved grant whose release-time IRS and sanctions checks pass
acceptance_criteria.then: payment proceeds; a DeepReviewExpired task is open; no new approvals for that charity proceed

acceptance_criteria.given: Two sponsors grant to the same charity
acceptance_criteria.then: one shared evidence record is read; two snapshots exist, one in each sponsor partition; neither sponsor can read the other's snapshot

acceptance_criteria.given: The TEOS/BMF source is unreachable and the cached observation is older than status_freshness_window
acceptance_criteria.then: outcome Unknown, grant held, no AI or human override path that bypasses the hold except a fresh observation

acceptance_criteria.given: A Type I supporting organization with no current donor-control certification

reason_for_change: The original wording makes 180-day reverification the currency standard and describes the execution-time check mainly as a sanctions check. Under Rev. Proc. 2018-32, reliance is assessed as of the grant date and the grantor must keep its own copy of the third-party report (§8.01). Shared evidence alone does not satisfy per-sponsor retention.
assumptions: A third-party data provider can supply all §8.01 fields with a timestamp
Sponsors accept shared evidence as an input subject to counsel opinion (Q2)
alternatives_considered: Keep 180-day currency and add sanctions only at release (rejected: loses grant-date reliance)
Live IRS lookup on every grant with no shared evidence (viable; higher latency, no deep-review reuse)
Per-sponsor full vetting (rejected: duplicates cost without legal benefit)
tradeoffs: Release-time lookup adds a dependency on data-source availability; mitigated by Hold-not-fail-open semantics

original_text: Retain all financial documents and substantiating financial evidence for **at least seven years**, with longer applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, sponsor or litigation-hold requirements taking precedence. This is a nonwaivable platform floor, not a legal conclusion that all records can be deleted after seven years. Retention clocks must be approved per record class; fund closure, donor death, advisor change and sponsor offboarding do not shorten retention. Originals and corrections remain immutable and linked; legal holds apply to existing and future matching evidence. Expiry triggers governed disposition review, never automatic deletion.
statement: Every stored record MUST be assigned exactly one retention class at creation. Each class MUST declare its authority (statute, regulation, contract, sponsor policy), trigger event, and minimum period. The effective retention of a record MUST be the maximum over all applicable classes, the platform floor (7 years from trigger, sponsor policy) and any legal hold. At minimum the catalog MUST include: OFAC/sanctions records (10 years from the transaction or screening decision, 31 CFR 501.601); tax-reliance snapshots (≥ the platform floor and until the related return period is closed, per counsel Q5); cost-basis and carryover records (until 7 years after the final disposition the record substantiates); and personal data not required as a financial record (deletable on request after its financial-record role ends). Expiry MUST create a disposition review task; deletion MUST NOT occur automatically.
business_objective: Make the 'longer obligation prevails' rule executable deterministically, and avoid both premature deletion and unlimited retention of personal data.
inputs: Record type, subject, sponsor, trigger events
processing_rules: Class assignment by record type is deterministic; unknown record type is rejected at write
effective_until = max(trigger+class period for all applicable classes, trigger+platform floor, hold release)
Trigger re-evaluated on correction or settlement events; never shortened by fund closure, donor death, advisor change or sponsor offboarding
Disposition requires an approved review by a role other than the requester
postconditions: No record with an active hold or unexpired class is deletable
Every record has exactly one primary class and a computed effective_until
failure_behavior: Catalog change: recompute asynchronously; until complete, deletion is blocked platform-wide
security: Disposition is an A4 reserved action; agents cannot approve
Sponsor offboarding exports do not remove Unbound's retained copy before effective_until
auditability: Class catalog versioned; each assignment records catalog version
Disposition evidence retained beyond the disposed record (metadata only)
configuration: Sponsors MAY lengthen any class; MUST NOT shorten below the platform floor or legal minimum

advisory: Propose class for a new record type for compliance review

ui_implications: Record detail shows retention class, authority and effective-until date
Disposition review list contains only expired, hold-free records
api_implications: Error: 423 Locked on delete of retained record
reporting_implications: Records by class and expiry month

acceptance_criteria.then: effective_until is no earlier than 2036-01-15 even though the platform floor would give 2033-01-15

acceptance_criteria.given: A fund closed in 2027 with contributions from 2026
acceptance_criteria.then: no contribution record of that fund is eligible for disposition

acceptance_criteria.given: A record whose classes have all expired and no hold
acceptance_criteria.then: a disposition review task opens; the record still exists until approved

acceptance_criteria.given: A new record type with no catalog entry
acceptance_criteria.then: the write is rejected with RetentionClassMissing

reason_for_change: The original makes 'longer requirements take precedence' a principle without naming any longer requirement. OFAC's 10-year rule (effective 2025-03-21) and §6001 'as long as material' for basis records are not represented, so the precedence clause is not executable.
assumptions: The platform floor remains an owner-directed 7 years
alternatives_considered: Single 10-year floor for everything (simpler, but over-retains personal data and conflicts with privacy deletion)
tradeoffs: A class catalog requires compliance ownership and maintenance

original_text: - **UNB-ACC-006:** Record contribution lifecycle from intent through receipt, valuation, restrictions, acceptance, acknowledgment, settlement and disposition, with distinct cash, securities and complex noncash treatments.
statement: The system MUST record each contribution as a state machine Declared → Received → Accepted → Valued → Acknowledged, with Settled and Disposed tracked as separate asset-level states for noncash property, and Rejected/Returned as terminal alternatives. It MUST NOT credit grantable fund balance before the contribution is Accepted and, for noncash property, before liquidation proceeds settle or the sponsor policy explicitly permits crediting at accepted value. It MUST issue a written acknowledgment for every contribution that (a) states the amount of cash or a description (not a value) of noncash property, (b) states whether any goods or services were provided and, if so, a good-faith estimate of their value, and (c) states that the sponsoring organization has exclusive legal control over the contributed assets (IRC 170(f)(18)(B)). For noncash property it MUST track Form 8283 Section B donee signature requests and every disposition within 3 years of receipt that requires a Form 8282 (filed within 125 days, copy to donor).
business_objective: Protect the donor's deduction and the sponsor's compliance, and prevent grants against unrealized or rejected contributions.
preconditions: Fund is Active and accepts contributions
Sponsor gift acceptance policy version active
inputs: Contribution intent (asset type, quantity/amount, donor, fund)
Valuation inputs (e.g., mean of high/low for publicly traded securities on date of gift, as sponsor policy defines)
processing_rules: Receipt is evidenced only by an external feed or verified document, never by donor declaration
Publicly traded securities: Received when shares arrive at the sponsor custodian account; acknowledgment describes shares, never a deductible value
Complex assets: Accepted only after gift-acceptance decision by an authorized human; AI may prepare the file
Acknowledgment issued once per contribution; corrections create a superseding acknowledgment linked to the original
Disposition within 3 years of receipt of Section B property creates a Form8282Due obligation with due date receipt-of-disposition + 125 days
Partial securities receipts: each lot is Received separately; acknowledgment waits for the declared quantity or a donor-confirmed final quantity
outputs: Balanced journal entries per posting rules
postconditions: Grantable balance never includes non-accepted or unsettled-noncash value unless policy explicitly allows
Every acknowledgment contains the 170(f)(18) control statement
failure_behavior: Feed shows fewer shares than declared: PartiallyReceived; donor notified; no acknowledgment until resolved
Returned ACH: reverse credit by linked entry; if already granted against, open a funding-shortfall case (no automatic clawback from charity)
Duplicate receipt evidence: idempotent on external reference; second is linked as duplicate, not credited
security: Donor sees only own contributions; advisor per delegated scope
auditability: Acknowledgment artifact hash, template version and data snapshot retained
configuration: Valuation method per asset class (sponsor policy)
Whether noncash may credit at accepted value before liquidation (sponsor policy, default: no)

advisory: Draft gift-acceptance memo for complex assets
Match unidentified incoming wires to declared intents with confidence
autonomous: Matching only when exact on amount, reference and sender account
prohibited: Assigning a deductible value to noncash property

reporting_implications: Schedule D Part I contribution aggregates

acceptance_criteria.then: contribution PartiallyReceived; 600 shares Received; no acknowledgment issued; fund grantable balance unchanged until acceptance and settlement policy satisfied

acceptance_criteria.given: The same custodian receipt message delivered twice
acceptance_criteria.then: one Received event; second recorded as duplicate; one journal entry
document states amount, 'no goods or services were provided' (or estimate), and the exclusive-legal-control statement

acceptance_criteria.given: Section B property received on 2026-03-01 and sold 2027-02-01
acceptance_criteria.then: a Form8282Due obligation exists with due date 2027-06-06 and donor-copy task

reason_for_change: The original lists lifecycle nouns but no ordering, no rule on when value becomes grantable, no acknowledgment content, and no Form 8282 tracking. Two developers could implement incompatible crediting rules.
alternatives_considered: Credit at declared value immediately (rejected: grants against unrealized assets)
tradeoffs: Waiting for settlement delays grantability for noncash gifts
regulatory_implications: Acknowledgment wording strictness (Keefer v. US) → counsel approval of templates
Form 8282 filing obligation is the sponsor's

original_text: - **UNB-PLAT-007:** **Strata** SHALL be used in the persistence architecture. All authoritative business history is append-only; corrections and reversals append new records. Physical storage guarantees and Strata integration must be verified.
statement: Authoritative business history MUST be stored by an Unbound-owned Ledger/Event Store component on managed PostgreSQL, in which authoritative tables are insert-only for the application role (no UPDATE/DELETE grants), corrections and reversals are new linked records, and each append is assigned a per-stream sequence number checked under optimistic concurrency. Strata MUST be used as the schema governance layer: every schema object for the authoritative store, including grants, triggers and row-level-security policies that enforce append-only and tenant isolation, MUST be declared in Strata source, deployed only through Strata plans, and checked for drift before each release; a 'not-compared' or 'unverifiable' Strata state for any such object MUST block release.
business_objective: Keep tamper-resistant, reconstructable financial and authority history without assuming capabilities Strata does not have.
processing_rules: Application role holds INSERT and SELECT only on authoritative tables
Append = (streamId, expectedVersion, events); mismatch → ConcurrencyConflict
Break-glass role use raises an incident and is logged outside the database
postconditions: No UPDATE or DELETE on authoritative tables by the application role
Drift report shows 'matches' for every governed object before release
failure_behavior: Drift detected in production: release blocked; incident opened
Strata reports not-compared for a policy: treated as failure, not pass
security: RLS policies by tenant on every authoritative table (see tenancy decision RCD-004)
auditability: Strata signed artifacts retained per release
Hash chain over each stream (Unbound-owned) for tamper evidence

advisory: Explain a Strata plan or drift report

ui_implications: not applicable: infrastructure requirement with no direct user interface
api_implications: Internal append API only; no external caller writes authoritative events directly

acceptance_criteria.when: it issues UPDATE on a journal table
acceptance_criteria.then: the database rejects it with permission denied

acceptance_criteria.given: A release candidate whose live database has a manually added trigger
Two concurrent appends to one fund stream at expectedVersion 7
acceptance_criteria.then: exactly one succeeds; the other receives ConcurrencyConflict and no partial events exist

reason_for_change: Strata (v0.1.1, pilot) is a declarative PostgreSQL schema management tool with no data API; it cannot provide append-only history, posting, temporal queries or replay. The original assigns these to Strata.
assumptions: Managed PostgreSQL 16 is acceptable for the authoritative store
alternatives_considered: Dedicated event-store product (adds a runtime dependency and ADR)
Do not use Strata (loses verified drift control)
tradeoffs: Unbound must build and test its own append, concurrency and hash-chain logic
regulatory_implications: not applicable: no direct legal obligation; supports audit evidence
